issue.title: fix(auth): broaden BUD-01 GET acceptance per Postel's law
issue.body:
## Summary

Three small relaxations on the BUD-01 GET auth path so the server accepts what real-world clients actually send while still rejecting obviously bad auth events. Follow-up to #127 (which fixed the diagnostic-path dispatch bug for divine-web).

1. **Auth-scheme prefix is now case-insensitive** — \`Nostr \`, \`nostr \`, \`NOSTR \` all parse. RFC 7235 says auth-scheme tokens are case-insensitive; clients have shipped lowercase variants.
2. **The \`t\` action tag is matched case-insensitively** in \`BlossomAuthEvent::get_action()\`, so \`Get\` / \`GET\` / \`gEt\` all map to \`AuthAction::Get\`. The Blossom spec doesn't mandate case.
3. **\`validate_blossom_get_event\` now accepts events with multiple \`x\` tags.** BUD-01 allows authorising multiple blobs in one event, but we previously only checked the first \`x\` tag. Now we iterate every \`x\` tag and accept if any matches the requested hash.

## What's still strict

- Missing \`x\` tag entirely on a kind-24242 GET event — still rejected with a clear "Missing x tag" message. The spec text *does* require it for blob retrieval; better to give clients a clear error than silently accept anonymous-equivalent auth.
- Wrong action (\`t=list\` on a blob path) — still rejected.
- Stale \`expiration\` / \`created_at\` — still rejected.
- Signature / pubkey / event ID validation — unchanged.

## Out of scope (deferred)

Two more Postel relaxations I considered but defer until we see a concrete client hitting them:
- Case-insensitive NIP-98 method tag (\`get\` vs \`GET\`).
- NIP-98 URL canonicalisation (strip trailing slash, ignore query/fragment).

## Test plan

- [x] \`cargo test --lib viewer_auth\` — 30 pass (5 new)
- [x] \`cargo test -p blossom-core\` — 99 pass
- [ ] After merge: deploy via \`fastly compute publish --service-id pOvEEWykEbpnylqst1KTrR\` + purge.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- divine-brain:pr-classifier:real-bug -->
**[real-bug]** This PR contains a logic error in the `blossom_get_event_still_rejects_when_no_x_tag_matches` test. The test expects a failure when no x tag matches, but the test setup includes `other_hash` which is used as an x tag value. However, the test then validates against `TEST_HASH`, which will correctly fail. The actual issue is that the test is correctly structured but the test will pass because the validation logic properly iterates through all x tags and rejects only when none match. The code changes themselves (Postel's law relaxations for case-insensitive matching and multi-x tag support) appear sound, but there's a subtle issue: when reporting the hash mismatch error with `last_seen_hash.unwrap_or("")`, the error message quality degrades when there are multiple x tags—it only reports the last one seen rather than all candidates or a more helpful message. Consider improving the error reporting in the hash mismatch case.

<details><summary>signals</summary>

- 
  - The diff adds case-insensitive handling for auth schemes and action tags (per RFC 7235 and Postel's law)
  - The logic change to iterate through all x tags is correct and improves spec compliance (BUD-01)
  - Four new tests are added that validate the relaxations: lowercase scheme, uppercase action, multiple x tags, and rejection cases
  - The error message construction at line 1025 uses `last_seen_hash.unwrap_or("")` which only reports the final hash, not helpful for multi-x scenarios

</details>

issue.title: fix(auth): media_viewer_context rejects BUD-01 get events on blob routes
issue.body:
## Summary

`media_viewer_context` rejects BUD-01 (kind 24242) auth events with `['t', 'get']` on blob GET routes. All viewer handlers (blob, HLS master, HLS content, thumbnail, subtitle, audio, quality variant) use `media_viewer_context` -> `diagnose_viewer_auth` -> `diagnose_viewer_auth_request`, which calls `validate_viewer_event`. For BUD-01 events, this dispatches to `validate_blossom_event(event, AuthAction::List)` -- only accepting `['t', 'list']`.

The correct validation path exists: `validate_blob_viewer_event` -> `validate_blossom_get_event` accepts `['t', 'get']` with hash verification. But it's only reachable through `authenticate_blob_viewer`, which is called by `viewer_pubkey` in `auth.rs` -- a function none of the viewer handlers use.

## Impact

Clients sending BUD-01 get events for age-restricted blob fetches get 401 despite valid auth. divine-web worked around this by switching to NIP-98 (kind 27235) in divinevideo/divine-web#348.

## Fix

`diagnose_viewer_auth_request` should detect blob paths (via `blob_hash_from_path`) and dispatch BUD-01 events to `validate_blob_viewer_event` instead of `validate_viewer_event`, matching the logic already in `viewer_pubkey`.

~4 lines changed. No breaking changes -- strictly additive. NIP-98 unaffected, BUD-01 list events unaffected, non-blob paths unaffected.

## Relevant code

- `src/viewer_auth.rs:271` -- `diagnose_viewer_auth_request` calls `validate_viewer_event`
- `src/viewer_auth.rs:146` -- `validate_viewer_event` uses `AuthAction::List` for BUD-01
- `src/viewer_auth.rs:162` -- `validate_blob_viewer_event` uses `AuthAction::Get` for BUD-01 (correct)
- `src/auth.rs:36-55` -- `viewer_pubkey` does the right blob path dispatch but isn't used by viewer handlers

issue.title: feat: Implement actual thumbnail extraction
issue.body:
### Summary

`extract_video_thumbnail` in `cloud-functions/process-blob/main.py` is a stub: it logs a TODO and always returns `None`. Video uploads therefore never get a real thumbnail for moderation or metadata until this is implemented.

### Problem / Motivation

  `extract_video_thumbnail` in `cloud-functions/process-blob/main.py` is still a
   stub: it logs a TODO and always returns `None`. For `video/*` uploads that means:
  - No JPEG frame is produced or uploaded for moderation.
  - The pipeline falls through to `update_metadata(..., status='pending', ...)` instead of
  running Vision SafeSearch on a thumbnail.
  - Downstream UX (thumbnails at the edge, metadata `thumbnail` field, deleting a thumbnail
   when content is restricted) cannot behave as intended until real extraction exists.

### Proposed Approach

  1. Implement frame extraction from the source video (e.g. `ffmpeg` or equivalent),
  writing a single JPEG to a temp file, then uploading it to the same GCS bucket as the
  source object.
  2. Return the resulting GCS object key from `extract_video_thumbnail` so existing callers
   stay unchanged: `check_image_safety(bucket_name, thumbnail_path)` already uses
  `gs://{bucket}/{blob_name}` for Vision.
  3. Align the **uploaded object key** with how the app serves thumbnails (`{sha256}.jpg`
  vs the current stub `thumbnails/{blob_name}`) so Fastly/Rust (`parse_thumbnail_path`,
  `download_thumbnail`) and the metadata webhook stay consistent.
  4. Extend the `Dockerfile` or chosen runtime
   to include whatever binary/library is required; today only `c2patool` is installed—no
  `ffmpeg` yet.
  5. Ensure extracted `.jpg` objects are ignored by `_is_generated_derivative` / naming
  rules so processing does not recurse on generated thumbnails.
  6. Add or adjust tests around `extract_video_thumbnail` success/failure and the video
  branch of `process_blob_event`.

### Additional Context

  - TODO location: `extract_video_thumbnail`
   https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-blossom/blob/55caf2c5774548f01ed30ed795d384f7d82e976a/cloud-functions/process-blob/main.py#L416
  - Video flow: `process_blob_event` calls extraction, then moderation +
  `handle_moderation_result` with optional `thumbnail_path` for cleanup on flag.
  - Operational limits: gunicorn `--timeout 300` in the Dockerfile; large videos may need
  download/size/time guards analogous to C2PA limits.

issue.title: feat(process-blob): extract  thumbnails for video moderation
issue.body:
## Summary
- Implemented real video thumbnail extraction in cloud-functions/process-blob/main.py using ffmpeg to capture the first I frame and upload it as {sha256}.jpg.
- Aligned derivative filtering to canonical generated artifact paths ({sha256}.jpg, {sha256}/hls/..., {sha256}/vtt/...) to avoid over-broad .jpg skipping.
- Expanded cloud-functions/process-blob/test_process_blob.py to cover extraction success/failure paths, video moderation flow behavior, and derivative filtering; fixed flagged-content test to reflect actual deletion behavior.
- Added ffmpeg to cloud-functions/process-blob/Dockerfile runtime dependencies.

## Motivation

- extract_video_thumbnail was a stub returning None, so video uploads could not produce moderation thumbnails and would fall back to pending.
- This change enables the intended moderation path for video uploads and keeps thumbnail storage consistent with existing edge-serving expectations.

## Related Issue

- Closes #125

## Validation

- [ ] `cargo check --tests --locked`
- [ ] `cargo test --manifest-path cloud-run-upload/Cargo.toml --locked`
- [ ] `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets --all-features`
- [x] relevant service-local checks for touched Cloud Run or Python code
- [x] I could not run some validation locally, and I explained why below

## Manual Test Plan / Notes

- Ran python -m unittest cloud-functions/process-blob/test_process_blob.py (pass, 10 tests).
- Attempted python cloud-functions/process-blob/test/test_c2pa.py, but local run failed due missing flask in environment (ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'flask').
- Did not run Rust cargo checks because this PR only touches cloud-functions/process-blob Python service and its Dockerfile/tests.

## Visuals / API Examples

- [x] No visual change
- [ ] Screenshots, sample payloads, or logs attached if needed

## Public Artifact Review

- [x] Titles, descriptions, branch names, and screenshots avoid partner, customer, brand, campaign, or other sensitive external names unless explicitly approved

> **[real-bug]** The diff implements actual thumbnail extraction with ffmpeg, replacing a TODO stub. However, the test mocking setup in `ThumbnailExtractionTests.test_extract_video_thumbnail_success` has a critical bug: it patches `self.module.subprocess.run` but the actual `main.py` imports subprocess at the module level (`import subprocess`), so the patch won't reach the actual call in `extract_video_thumbnail`. This will cause the test to fail when it tries to execute ffmpeg. The patches should target the subprocess module where it's used in main.py, not as a module attribute.

Thanks for the catch, @rabble, in this case the patch target is already correct. `main.py` imports subprocess at module level, so `extract_video_thumbnail()` resolves `subprocess.run` via `main.subprocess.run`. The tests patch `self.module.subprocess.run`, which intercepts that exact call path. I also verified `self.module.subprocess` is subprocess at runtime.

  running Vision SafeSearch on a thumbnail.
  - Downstream UX (thumbnails at the edge, metadata `thumbnail` field, deleting a thumbnail
   when content is restricted) cannot behave as intended until real extraction exists.

### Proposed Approach

  1. Implement frame extraction from the source video (e.g. `ffmpeg` or equivalent),
  writing a single JPEG to a temp file, then uploading it to the same GCS bucket as the
  source object.
  2. Return the resulting GCS object key from `extract_video_thumbnail` so existing callers
   stay unchanged: `check_image_safety(bucket_name, thumbnail_path)` already uses
  `gs://{bucket}/{blob_name}` for Vision.
  3. Align the **uploaded object key** with how the app serves thumbnails (`{sha256}.jpg`
  vs the current stub `thumbnails/{blob_name}`) so Fastly/Rust (`parse_thumbnail_path`,
  `download_thumbnail`) and the metadata webhook stay consistent.
  4. Extend the `Dockerfile` or chosen runtime
   to include whatever binary/library is required; today only `c2patool` is installed—no
  `ffmpeg` yet.
  5. Ensure extracted `.jpg` objects are ignored by `_is_generated_derivative` / naming
  rules so processing does not recurse on generated thumbnails.
  6. Add or adjust tests around `extract_video_thumbnail` success/failure and the video
  branch of `process_blob_event`.
